tecnicas.observacao: Pacote focal: prompt de preenchimento (infill) para CodeT5-large com cinco partes (informação externa = template de correção recuperado e aplicado à linha defeituosa com o marcador <INFILL>; informação interna = comentário 'use [DONOR] in the next line:' com um identificador doador recuperado do mesmo arquivo; linha defeituosa como comentário; contexto antes e depois). contexto = linha defeituosa, contexto circundante, template recuperado e identificador doador; restricoes = template aplicado que fixa a forma e o local da edição (<INFILL>); instrucao = diretiva em linguagem natural 'use [DONOR] in the next line'; amostragem = vários prompts (um por identificador entre os top-5), 5.000 amostras por erro e seleção por validação com testes. Contrafactual de pacote: 'No Retrieval' (só o LLM base) contra o sistema completo na Tabela II. Pacote híbrido: inclui recuperação por BM-25 e CoCoSoDa, filtragem por análise estática (Pylint/Pyright), validação por testes e orçamento de 5.000 amostras/5 h; o ganho não é atribuível a um único mecanismo. citacoes.trecho: In this paper, we introduce RetypeR, an integrated retrieval-based framework to repair Python type errors automatically.

To integrate the information retrieved from the aforementioned external and internal stages, RetypeR constructs context-aware repair prompts for LLMs to guide them in generating correct patches for type errors.
The context-aware repair prompts include five parts: the external information, the internal information, the buggy line, the context before and the context after the buggy line, as shown in Figure 3.
The placeholder token <INFILL> signals to the model the precise location where new code should be generated according to the applied template.
Each repair prompt includes only one donor code identifier.
To repair each bug, we sample the model 5,000 times and set a five-hour timeout limit following previous study [13].
Subsequently, it executes the test suites on each patch to identify the plausible patches that successfully pass all the test suites.
Following common APR practice, we conduct thorough manual evaluations of each plausible patch to determine its accuracy as a correct patch.
We use the OpenAI API of ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) and Codex (code-davinci-002) for evaluation, invoking these models using the same prompt from the prior work [12].
Specifically, we begin with a scenario where no retrieval stage is applied, meaning both the external and internal retrieval stages of RetypeR are ablated, and only the base LLM is used.
Moreover, when considering the entire project, some identifier tokens unrelated to the repair may achieve high rankings, introducing more noise [16].
Following prior work [16], and due to the high cost of APR, we focus on the pandas project within the TypeBugs benchmark which has the largest number of type errors.

Due to the limitation of computational resources, we only explored the case of directly fusing the retrieval ranking results of lexical-aware and semantic-aware retrieval modules employing the RRF strategy.
To mitigate this concern, we conduct experiments on two different benchmarks, TypeBugs and BugsInPy, and demonstrate that RetypeR achieves state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks.
TypeFix [12] is the state-of-the-art approach for fixing Python type errors, which mines fix templates by hierarchical clustering and applies these templates as domain knowledge for patch generation.
